Carmen: quick question — trying to lock down the embeddings endpoint behavior for mixed/edge inputs. want to confirm the intended contract for: empty strings, explicit nulls, non-string JSON objects, truncation semantics, and batch-size handling. example payload below. any quick clarifications?

Carmen: ```json
{
  "inputs": ["hello", "", null, {"title": "ok"}, "a very long string..." ]
}
```

alice: short answers: preserve input order; return one item per input; null inputs -> return `null` entry; empty string -> return an embedding for the empty string (not null). non-strings -> we stringify before embedding (so object -> `JSON.stringify(obj)`).

ben: truncation rules: we truncate by UTF-8 byte length, not characters. current internal limit for a single input is 65_536 bytes (64KB). if truncated, we append a marker `\u241F` (unit separator) at truncation boundary so callers can detect. we should document this clearly.

devon: batch size: server accepts up to 1024 items per request (practical limit). if a request exceeds that we return 413 + body: `{"error": "batch_too_large", "max_items": 1024}`. also note token/byte quotas still apply per item even inside a batch.

alice: response shape example (keeps order, nulls preserved):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...], "index": 0},
    {"embedding": [0.0, 0.0, ...], "index": 1},
    null,
    {"embedding": [0.12, 0.5, ...], "index": 3},
    {"embedding": [0.003, -0.01, ...], "index": 4}
  ],
  "embedding_dim": 3072
}
```

carmen: thanks — couple followups: 1) is embedding_dim fixed per model in the API response? 2) are we ok with the `index` field vs relying purely on array order? 3) will we ever compress empty-string embeddings to a canonical zero vector or keep model's output?

ben: 1) yes, `embedding_dim` is included (model-specific) and guaranteed stable for a given model version. 2) array order is the source of truth; `index` is just convenience for clients that do parallel processing. don't rely on `index` to change ordering. 3) we keep the model's output for empty string — deterministic but not forced to zeros.

devon: infra-bot note: if any item bytesize > 64KB we reject the item-level request with 422 and the response will contain `failed_indices` with offending indexes. bulk behavior: if any item fails pre-flight (oversize/non-string after coercion), we respond 207 Multi-Status with per-item status. ops prefers explicit per-item errors instead of dropping entire batch.

alice: action items: (A) docs PR to clarify: coercion rules, truncation marker, 64KB limit, 1024 batch cap, null/empty semantics. (B) sdk: add helpers to `coerceToString(input)` and to expose `failed_indices` handling. (C) runtime: ensure we emit telemetry metric `embed.request.truncations` when truncation happens.

carmen: perfect. I'll open the docs PR and tag you all. pinging @alice for SDK changes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: noted: created issue INF-4483 for per-item rejection behavior and INF-4484 for truncation telemetry.

ben: one more note — we should add an integration test with mixed inputs and assert null-preservation + returned `embedding_dim` matches model manifest.

carmen: agreed, will add test in eng-ml/tests and link in the PR.
